planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Brilliant is one of the older Southern Indica selections long grown in Gulf Coast nursery trade for its saturated bloom color.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with protection from hot afternoon sun. Brilliant is a classic Southern Indica azalea that has been grown in Deep South gardens for generations, valued for its vivid orange-red single flowers produced in an overwhelming spring flush on a large, vigorous evergreen shrub. Like other Southern Indica selections, it traces to the original Indica hybrids brought into the Gulf Coast nursery trade in the 19th century and remains a dependable large-scale landscape and hedging plant in older gardens. Water deeply during dry spells, especially while establishing, and prune lightly right after flowering if shaping is needed, since flower buds for the following year set soon after bloom ends.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Hexe is one of the historic Kurume azalea selections long cultivated in Western gardens for its intensely colored small flowers.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade with good air circulation. Hexe is one of the classic Kurume azalea selections, prized for over a century for its dense, twiggy, compact habit and its profusion of small, deep magenta-crimson hose-in-hose flowers that all but cover the plant during the spring flush. Its fine-textured small leaves and tight mounding form give it the refined, formal look typical of the best Kurume types, making it useful for foundation plantings and mass borders. Water deeply during dry spells, especially while establishing, and prune lightly right after flowering if shaping is needed, since flower buds for next year's bloom set soon after the spring flush ends.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Sherwood Orchid is a Kurume-type selection from Sherwood Nursery, a sister introduction to the widely grown Sherwood Red.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade with good air circulation. Sherwood Orchid produces a heavy spring flush of orchid-pink hose-in-hose flowers on a dense, compact, mounding Kurume-type shrub, sharing the tight, twiggy habit and fine small foliage typical of the group. It was introduced alongside its better-known sister seedling Sherwood Red, and the two are still often sold together as a contrasting pair for foundation plantings and mixed azalea borders. Water deeply during dry spells, especially while establishing, and prune lightly right after flowering if shaping is needed, since flower buds for next year's bloom set soon after the spring flush ends.

common_name: Eikan Azalea (White Pink-Striped Satsuki Bonsai Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Eikan is a classic late-blooming Satsuki azalea popular in Japan both as a landscape plant and as a bonsai subject.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade under filtered light. Eikan bears large white flowers heavily striped, flecked, and edged in pink, with considerable variation in pattern from bloom to bloom on the same low, spreading Satsuki azalea, blooming weeks after Kurume and Southern Indica types have finished. Its late season, showy variegated flowers, and tolerance of pruning have made it a long-favored cultivar for bonsai training as well as low borders and rock gardens. Prune immediately after bloom, since flower buds set on the current season's growth and later pruning removes next year's flowers.

common_name: Kinsai Azalea (Spidery Narrow-Petaled Red Satsuki Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Kinsai is a distinctive Satsuki azalea grown for its narrow, spidery, strap-shaped petals, popular in Japan for bonsai.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade under filtered light. Kinsai is grown for its unusual narrow, ribbon-like, spidery red petals, a striking departure from the broad overlapping petals of most azaleas, borne on a low, dense Satsuki shrub that blooms late in the season after Kurume and Southern Indica types have finished. The distinctive strap-petaled flower form has long made it a favorite subject for bonsai training in Japan, though it performs equally well as an unclipped low border or rock garden shrub. Prune immediately after bloom, since flower buds set on the current season's growth and later pruning removes next year's flowers.
